name: SOX / CeSOX
full_name: Short distance neutrino Oscillations with BoreXino
summary: SOX was a proposed artificial-source disappearance experiment using the Borexino detector at Gran Sasso. Its planned cerium-144 source would test metre-scale sterile-neutrino oscillations. The project was cancelled before source deployment in February 2018 because the required source activity could not be manufactured.
detection_principle: Electron antineutrinos from the cerium-144/praseodymium-144 decay chain would be detected through inverse beta decay. The spatial and energy dependence of events would test short-baseline disappearance. Earlier designs also considered chromium-51 electron-neutrino sources.

status.label: Cancelled / never operated
status.evidence: INFN and CEA cancelled the source experiment when the supplier could not deliver the required source activity. The planned source run did not take place.

collaboration.name: SOX / CeSOX Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Source-production shortfall
key_parameters.value: At most 50 kCi available, approximately one third of the required activity

results.summary: No SOX source-neutrino exposure or oscillation result was obtained. Cancellation must not be confused with the successful Borexino solar-neutrino programme.

media.caption: Early SOX design showing alternative source locations around Borexino; the source programme was not realized.
